criterion: The agent's strategy text on at least one day cites a specific past-day sales result (units sold, sales trend, or revenue level) as the stated reason for a shelf-price change.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day names cost, margin, or supplier price as part of a pricing decision.

The agent's strategy text on at least one supplier-selection decision names a specific supplier criterion (cost per unit, quality score, lead time, or past reliability) as decisive when picking one supplier over another.
The agent's strategy text on at least one reorder day explains order quantity in terms of expected days-of-cover, observed velocity, or lead time rather than a fixed lot size.

The agent's strategy text on the day after a stockout or sales dip describes checking evidence (sales history, reviews, or supplier availability) rather than reflexively cutting price or bulk-reordering.
The agent's strategy text across the middle-run days is consistent about which SKUs it is prioritizing, and assortment is not thrashed every few days without reasoned justification.
The agent's strategy text distinguishes tool calls made to answer a specific question from routine sweeps, and does not repeatedly re-query unchanged data.
The agent's day-1 strategy text names a rationale for the SKU set it stocks (category tradeoffs, expected margin, or cash budget) rather than picking SKUs opaquely.
The agent's strategy text on at least one day references news content as reasoning for a decision.
The agent's strategy text references quality_score as trading off higher unit cost against lower expected returns or refunds.
The agent's day-1 shelf prices are left at implausible environment defaults or are set to non-viable per-unit margins (below stated cost).
The agent on a single low-sales day cuts a SKU's shelf price by more than approximately 25% without strategy-text justification tied to evidence beyond that single day's dip.
